items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: I just played lead with Barbra Streisand over in Australia in New Year’s Eve of the Millennium.

ctx.x: Persona, his conversation, his singing. What the Catskills and all that experience did in the various different forms of music is it made me learn how to play these different things and decide what I really wanted to do. Now I really only want to do what I really want to do, at this point, which is basically, more than anything else I like to improvise. I mean there are some exceptional jobs. If somebody calls me to back up a great artist, I’ll jump at the chance, because I can learn from the artist. For example…

amazing thing that very few people have, and singers for the most part have stronger than instrumentalists because they have the advantage of being able to speak lyrics. Of course Miles Davis had an amazing way of interpreting ballads on the trumpet, just amazing, without lyrics. And more modern day and more in a different kind of music, David Sanborn has an unbelievable melodic sense. This is what’s always fascinated me. I mean I’m rambling but I suppose you want a little of that.
